--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.random_walk()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Perform a random walk on the graph. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.random_walk()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Perform a random walk on the graph. title: >- [Graph.random_walk()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Perform a random walk on the graph. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Perform a random walk on the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L64603-L64792){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.random_walk( source, steps, mode="out", stuck="return", seed=None, weighted=None, attr_name=None, return_list=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Random walk](../assets/graphs/random-walk.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A directed house-shaped graph walked from A for 6 steps with a fixed seed. Filled badges give each node's positions in the walk, 0 for the start; A and B are visited twice. The card lists the 7 visited nodes, A, B, C, A, B, D, E; edge E to C is unused." width="100%"} Takes a random walk starting from a given node, choosing the next node at random at each step: uniformly among the neighbors, or, with `weighted=`, in proportion to the weight of the edges leading to each neighbor. Can return the visit order as a list of node IDs, or store the position of each node in the walk as a node attribute for visualization. The walk follows edges according to the `mode=` parameter: - `"out"`: follow outgoing edges (the default) - `"in"`: follow incoming edges (reverse direction) - `"all"`: ignore edge directions (treat as undirected) On an undirected graph all three modes behave the same. If the walk reaches a node with no valid neighbors (gets 'stuck'), behavior is controlled by the `stuck=` parameter. Random walks are useful for: - sampling nodes from a large graph in proportion to how well connected they are - generating node sequences for embedding methods such as DeepWalk or Node2Vec - simulating diffusion, browsing, or foraging processes on a network Time complexity: `O(steps)` with `O(degree)` neighbor lookups per step for `mode="out"`; `"in"` and `"all"` scan the adjacency of every node at each step, so they cost `O(n)` per step. A weighted walk first gathers every node's weighted neighbors in one pass over the edges, then costs `O(degree)` per step in any mode. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node where the walk begins, given as an integer node ID or a string label. [steps]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of moves to make. A complete walk visits `steps + 1` nodes, counting the start node. With `steps=0` the walk is just `[source]`. [mode]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["out"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Which edges the walker may follow from each node: `"out"` (default) follows outgoing edges, `"in"` follows incoming edges backwards, and `"all"` follows edges in either direction. Only matters for directed graphs. [stuck]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["return"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : What to do when the walker reaches a node with no edge it can follow under `mode=`. With `"return"` (default), the walk stops there and the partial walk is used. With `"error"`, a `RuntimeError` is raised instead. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator. The same seed on the same graph always produces the same walk. If `None` (default), the walk is seeded from system entropy and differs from call to call. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, step from a node to each neighbor with probability proportional to the total weight of the edges joining them (`1` where missing), so parallel edges add up. Zero-weight edges are never followed, a node whose usable edges all weigh zero counts as stuck, and negative weights raise an error. This matches the `weight=` argument of NetworkX's `random_walk()`. If `False`, every neighbor is equally likely. If `None` (default), follows whether the graph was created as weighted. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute that receives each node's position in the walk. If `None` (default), the attribute is called `random_walk_order`. Positions are 0-indexed, so the start node gets `0`. A node visited several times keeps the position of its *last* visit; nodes never visited get no value. Ignored when `return_list=True`. [return_list]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `False` (default), store the positions as a node attribute (see `attr_name=`) and return the graph for method chaining. If `True`, leave node attributes untouched and return the list of visited node IDs. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[list[int], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_list=` is `True`: list of node IDs visited in walk order, of length `steps + 1` (includes the starting node). May be shorter if `stuck="return"` and the walk terminates early. If `return_list=` is `False`: returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `source=` is a label or integer ID that does not exist, `mode=` is not one of `"out"`, `"in"`, `"all"`, `stuck=` is not `"return"` or `"error"`, or a weighted walk meets a negative edge weight. [RuntimeError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If walk gets stuck and `stuck="error"`. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Random walks are the substrate under an enormous slice of graph algorithms. PageRank and personalized PageRank interpret each score as the stationary probability of a walker biased by teleportation; Node2Vec, DeepWalk, and related graph embeddings feed sampled walks straight into skip-gram; Walktrap community detection reasons about how long walks tend to stay in a community; and countless sketching and sampling routines lean on walk mixing times to bound their guarantees. On directed graphs the `mode=` argument decides which edges the walker can traverse, which is essential when reversibility is not guaranteed. Setting `seed=` locks in reproducibility, and `stuck='return'` lets the walk terminate gracefully at a sink instead of raising. ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~random_edge_walk`) : A random walk that records the edges crossed. [](`~random_walk_with_restart`) : Visit probabilities for a walk that keeps returning to its seeds. [](`~generate_random_paths`) : Many short random walks at once. ## Examples {.doc-examples} On a cycle, every step goes one way or the other. A walk of 10 steps visits 11 nodes, and the same `seed=` gives the same walk: ::: {#b58cc45e .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec cycle = ec.Graph().add_cycle_graph(6) cycle.random_walk(1, steps=10, seed=23, return_list=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [1, 2, 3, 2, 1, 6, 5, 6, 1, 2, 1] ``` ::: ::: On a directed graph the walk follows the arrows. When it reaches a node with no way out, here `C`, it stops early: ::: {#ff313830 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph.from_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C")], directed=True) graph.random_walk("A", steps=10, return_list=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [1, 2, 3] ``` ::: ::: ### Where a walker spends its time `karate_club()` links the 34 members of a university karate club who met outside the club, before it split in two. A walker who moves to a random friend at each step spends time at each member in proportion to the member's number of friends: over 10,000 steps, about a tenth of its visits are to the instructor (`0`), who has 16 of the 156 friends counted at both ends: ::: {#a535608c .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} from collections import Counter karate = ec.karate_club() visits = Counter( karate.random_walk(1, steps=10_000, seed=1, return_list=True) ) { karate.get_label_from_id(n): (visits[n], karate.get_degree(n)) for n in [1, 34, 33, 12] } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {'0': (1064, 16), '33': (1035, 17), '32': (744, 12), '11': (61, 1)} ``` ::: ::: ::: {#cb57a6fa .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} karate = karate.set_node_attrs("visits", dict(visits)) karate.plot( size_by="visits", color_by="faction", label_by="label", seed=1 ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
